addendum6.notes: cannot-express-4x, proved from the head-drop kernel own storage algebra rather than measured on the model. C10 stored count is 1024*k*64 + 1024*k*64 + numel(k_proj) + numel(v_proj) = 131072*k + 1048576 for k surviving query heads, because a dropped query head does not stop the child storing the key and value projections -- the kernel reports dead_kv_groups and deliberately does NOT bank the rows it could then drop, since claiming a saving the installed child does not take is exactly the storage dishonesty ADDENDUM 6 6.2 exists to catch. The S4 budget is 0.25 x 3,145,728 = 786,432. The k_proj/v_proj floor alone is 1,048,576, so even k=0 stores 0.333x and NO head count satisfies S4. The harness refused it from its own count at the planned width: C10.T1.S4.L02 stores 1835008 against a bound of 786432 at width 384. Note the planner suggested that width because the registry falls through to the generic factor-pair model for (T1, C10), which is the wrong algebra for a head drop; the ENFORCED number is the kernel own and it is the one that refuses. The measurable rung is S2: C10.T1.S2.L02 drops sixteen heads to four -- a real 4x of head COUNT -- stores exactly 0.5x and scores 8 of 15 alive-degraded.
